identity.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction

problem.claim: Develop an autoregressive paradigm for scalable visual generation and learning.

contributions.claim: Introduces Visual AutoRegressive modeling (VAR), reformulating image autoregression as coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction rather than raster-scan next-token prediction.
Reports that VAR improves autoregressive image generation across quality, speed, data efficiency, and scalability dimensions.
Releases VAR models and code for further exploration of autoregressive visual generation and unified learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present VAR as a new generation paradigm and report that it is the first GPT-style autoregressive approach to surpass diffusion transformers in image generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On ImageNet 256×256, the authors report FID improving from 18.65 to 1.73, IS from 80.4 to 350.2, and inference becoming approximately 20× faster than the AR baseline.
The authors report that VAR outperforms DiT in image quality, inference speed, data efficiency, and scalability.
The authors report near−0.998 linear correlation coefficients for VAR scaling laws and zero-shot results on in-painting, out-painting, and editing.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper replaces raster-scan next-token prediction with coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction for image autoregression.
The authors report large ImageNet gains in FID, IS, and inference speed over an AR baseline.
They report advantages over DiT, power-law scaling, and zero-shot downstream image-editing capabilities.
Models and code are released to support further VAR and AR research.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a specific architectural reframing—next-scale prediction—with benchmark metrics, cross-model comparisons, scaling-law analysis, and downstream-task demonstrations.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more informative when evidence tests distinct promised properties rather than only one headline metric.
lessons.application: For a new generative method, map each claimed property to a corresponding evaluation: core quality, efficiency, scaling behavior, and transfer or zero-shot use.
lessons.exception: This mapping may be unsuitable when the method targets only one narrowly defined capability or when the relevant evaluations are unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify VAR and DiT configurations, datasets beyond ImageNet for the main benchmark, statistical variability, or detailed evaluation protocols.
The scaling-law setup and zero-shot task protocols are not described, so the reported correlations and generalization scope cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
